about: The cases of the optional syntax and of the HTML the panel draws. Each example comes from the program or specification that writes it. `syntax` is the setting it belongs to (tandemMarkdown.syntax.<id>), or null for standard markdown. `value`, for a setting with choices, is the value the case is read under, and `off` the value that turns it off. `nodes` are the parser's nodes for the construct, in order, with the syntax on (none of them is there with it off). `view` is the text Rich view shows, and `drawn` counts what the reader sees, by kind: each name is a kind in src/panel/syntax/kinds.ts, which says how the page draws it, and the count is how many a reader would count (each box once, nested ones too, however many lines it takes). `cursor`, when given, is a piece of the example whose source shows once the cursor is inside it in Rich editor. `plain`, when given, lists pieces of the example that look exactly like the text around them: in Rich editor with the cursor inside each, and in Rich view where Rich view shows them. `off` is what Rich view shows with the syntax off, when that is not the example as typed. `reference`, when given, makes the example an entry of SYNTAX.md: its `group` (standard, github, notes, documents, html, math, or typed and wrong for what is shown as typed and drawn wrongly), its `title`, what it `becomes` in a sentence or two of markdown, and the programs that write it (`writers`); scripts/syntax-reference.mjs writes the file from them. Read by test/panel/syntax/cases.test.ts, test/panel/syntax/reference.test.ts and harness/tests/syntax.spec.mjs.

cases.name: a tag and a nested tag

reference.title: Tags
reference.becomes: A label. Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on a Mac) searches the workspace for it. By Obsidian's rule a color code such as `#ff0000` is a tag, and a number such as `#123` is not.

cases.name: a tag at the start of a line
a color code is a tag
letters in any script make a tag, and punctuation ends one
a number after # stays text
# inside a word or an address stays text
an escaped # stays text
a tag in code stays code
a heading's mark is not a tag
emoji codes on GitHub's list

reference.title: Emoji codes
reference.becomes: The emoji, for the names on GitHub's list, with its code as a tooltip. A time such as `12:30:45` stays text.

cases.name: emoji codes made of digits and signs
a time stays text
a name not on the list stays text
an emoji typed as itself stays as typed
an emoji code in code stays code
a GitHub alert

reference.title: Alerts
reference.becomes: A colored box with its type's icon and name: `NOTE`, `TIP`, `IMPORTANT`, `WARNING` or `CAUTION`.

cases.name: GitHub's other four alerts
cases.example:
> [!TIP]
> Tip text.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Key text.

> [!WARNING]
> Warn text.

> [!CAUTION]
> Careful text.
cases.view:
Tip
Tip text.

Important
Key text.

Warning
Warn text.

Caution
Careful text.
cases.off:
[!TIP]
Tip text.

[!IMPORTANT]
Key text.

[!WARNING]
Warn text.

[!CAUTION]
Careful text.

cases.name: a callout with a title, in lower case
a callout folded by its sign

reference.title: Callouts
reference.becomes: A colored box of one of Obsidian's thirteen types and their aliases, with its title. A `-` after the type starts it folded and a `+` open, and a click on its arrow opens and closes it. Callouts nest.

cases.name: a callout open by its sign
an alias takes its type's look
a callout inside a callout
a type no program knows takes the note's look and its own name
a marker after other text stays a quote
math in a line

reference.title: Math in a line
reference.becomes: A formula, drawn by KaTeX. Prices stay text: `$5 and $10` is not a formula, by the rule Pandoc and VS Code's preview follow.

cases.name: two prices stay text
cases.example: The pots cost $5 and the pans cost $10.
cases.view: The pots cost $5 and the pans cost $10.

cases.name: prices with thousands stay text
a closing dollar before a digit is not one
an opening dollar before a space is not one
escaped dollars stay text
GitHub's backtick form

reference.title: Math in a line with backticks
reference.becomes: A formula in the line.

cases.name: display math inside a line
a math block

reference.title: Math blocks
reference.becomes: A formula on its own lines. Its pencil, or the cursor, opens its source, with the drawing kept beneath while you edit.

cases.name: a math code block

reference.title: Math code blocks
reference.becomes: A formula on its own lines, as a math block is drawn.

cases.name: dollars in code stay code
wikilinks
cases.view: See Other note and an alias.

reference.title: Wikilinks
reference.becomes: A link to the note, found by the end of its path, showing the text after the bar when there is one. Typing `[[` offers notes.

cases.name: wikilinks to a heading and to a block of a note
cases.view: Other note > Part two and Other note > ^quote-1

reference.title: Wikilinks to a heading or a block
reference.becomes: A link to that heading, or to the block with that id, in the note.

cases.name: Bear's link to a heading goes to the heading when no note answers it as a folder path
cases.example: See [[Other note/Part two]] and [[Other note/Part three|the end]].
cases.view: See Other note > Part two and the end.

reference.title: Bear's links to headings
reference.becomes: A link to the heading "Part two" in the note "Other note", as Bear means it, when no note "Part two" sits in a folder "Other note" and the note "Other note" has that heading. When a note answers the folder path, the link goes to it, as Obsidian and Foam read it.

cases.name: a slash link that a note answers as a folder path stays a link to that note
a slash link to a heading the note does not have is missing
wikilinks in front matter values are links

reference.title: Wikilinks in front matter
reference.becomes: Links in the front matter's table, opened as other links are.

cases.name: highlight

reference.title: Highlight
reference.becomes: Highlighted text.

cases.name: a footnote and its note

reference.title: Footnotes
reference.becomes: The reference shows its note's number, counted in the order the notes are first referred to, as GitHub counts them, and the note shows the same number. Pointing at a reference shows the note's text, and it opens as a link does, going to the note and back.

cases.name: key caps

reference.title: Keys
reference.becomes: Key caps. As with all HTML in a line, the tags are hidden until the cursor is in them.

cases.name: subscript and superscript

reference.title: Subscript and superscript in HTML
reference.becomes: Subscript and superscript.

cases.name: underline, mark and a span, whose style is dropped as GitHub drops it
cases.view: An underlined, marked and plain word.

reference.title: Underline, highlight and spans
reference.becomes: Underlined and highlighted text. A `style` is dropped, as GitHub drops it.

cases.name: a line break

reference.title: Line breaks in HTML
reference.becomes: A line break.

cases.name: a picture in a line

reference.title: Pictures in HTML
reference.becomes: The picture, at the size its attributes give.

cases.name: a named anchor is hidden

reference.title: Anchors
reference.becomes: Hidden. A link to `#here` goes to it.

cases.name: tag-shaped text that is not an element stays as typed

reference.title: Text shaped like a tag
reference.becomes: Shown as typed when it names no HTML element, where GitHub would show nothing.

cases.name: an element GitHub refuses shows as code

reference.title: HTML elements GitHub refuses
reference.becomes: Shown as typed, faded. GitHub refuses them too.
